name: Real-time insurance underwriting & claims fraud at FNOL
category: New — insurance underwriting and claims-fraud at first-notice-of-loss
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Real-time insurance underwriting and claims-fraud at First Notice of Loss (FNOL), covering per-policyholder behavioral session telemetry at quote bind and at claim intake across P&C, auto, home, pet, life and health lines.
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A P&C, auto, home or health insurer's underwriting and SIU (Special Investigations Unit) teams must score a quote, bind, endorsement or first-notice-of-loss event in seconds to a few minutes using per-policyholder, per-device, per-vehicle and per-property behavioural and velocity features, and emit a fraud / risk score that gates auto-pay, manual review or step-up investigation before the claim or policy is bound or paid.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: Three concrete jobs: (1) Score every quote and bind in real time for application-fraud — apps-per-device, apps-per-email-domain, apps-per-VIN, apps-per-property-address, prior-quote velocity, repeated-cancel-rebind patterns, ghost-broker scripts hammering the rate-quote endpoint — exactly the 'shut the front door' problem SAS and Insly describe and that FRISS' underwriting product targets at point-of-sale. (2) Score every FNOL inside the digital claim flow before auto-pay — Lemonade's AI Jim reads location, date/time, time-on-question, answer-revision history, video tone, facial micro-expressions and prior-claim recency to either auto-pay in seconds or escalate; this is the canonical FNOL pattern Shift, Friss, Charlee.ai and Carpe Data are all selling agentic versions of in 2025–2026. (3) Drive continuous (not point-in-time) underwriting risk by ingesting telematics, smart-home, wearable and IoT signals — Root's UBI score over billions of driving miles, Hippo's smart-home sensor stream, Progressive Snapshot, John Hancock Vitality — and serve the aggregated per-policy / per-vehicle / per-property feature vector to the pricing and step-up-investigation models.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical @bv.event records: quote_request {ts, applicant_id, email_hash, email_domain, phone_hash, device_id, ip, ua_hash, line_of_business, state, vin_hash, property_address_hash, prior_carrier_hash, claimed_dob_year, requested_coverage, channel, agent_id}, bind_attempt {ts, applicant_id, policy_id, premium, payment_method_token, device_id, ip}, policy_endorsement {ts, policy_id, change_type, delta_premium, ts_relative_to_loss_seconds}, fnol_started {ts, policy_id, claim_id, channel(web|mobile|voice|agent), device_id, ip, ua_hash, loc_geohash, loc_h3}, fnol_field_event {ts, claim_id, field_name, dwell_ms, edits, paste_event, backspace_count}, fnol_completed {ts, claim_id, loss_date, loss_type, loss_geohash, claimed_amount, photo_count, video_present, voice_present}, photo_upload {ts, claim_id, exif_ts, exif_geohash, exif_device_model, perceptual_hash, ela_score, exif_tamper_flag, file_bytes}, voice_segment {ts, claim_id, segment_seq, voice_stress_score, pitch_band, transcript_hash, sentiment_score}, behavioral_signal {ts, session_id, claim_id|quote_id, mouse_velocity_px_s, keystroke_dwell_ms, keystroke_flight_ms, hesitation_count, tab_switches}, telematics_trip_window {ts, policy_id, vin_hash, trip_id, miles, hard_brake_count, hard_accel_count, phone_handling_count, night_minutes, speed_band_distribution}, smart_home_signal {ts, policy_id, property_id, sensor_type, alert_code} (Hippo-shape), wearable_signal {ts, policy_id, member_id, hr_band, steps_band} (John Hancock Vitality-shape), claim_decision {ts, claim_id, decision(auto_pay|review|deny|siu_escalate), score, model_version, features_snapshot_id, reason_codes}, siu_outcome {ts, claim_id, fraud_confirmed, recovery_amount}. PII is hashed (email_hash, phone_hash, vin_hash, property_address_hash) so beava state is keyed by tokens, not raw PII.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Per-entity aggregations expressed as beava @bv.table primitives. Per applicant_id / policyholder_id: count(quotes, 1h/24h/7d/30d), count(prior_claims, 90d/365d/3y), velocity(claim_amount, 30d/365d), n_unique(device_id, 90d), n_unique(ip, 30d), days-since-last-claim, days-since-bind (a 30-day-old policy filing a total-loss is a classic flag), distribution(loss_type, lifetime). Per device_id: n_unique(policyholder_id, 1h/24h/7d/30d), count(quotes, 24h/7d), count(claims, 30d/365d) — the headline 'one device, many policyholders' synthetic-identity signal. Per email_domain: count(quotes, 1h/24h/7d), distinct applicant_id count (24h), failure_ratio — surfaces disposable-domain bursts. Per ip and per (ip_subnet, 24h): n_unique(applicant_id, 24h), n_unique(device_id, 24h) — the SEON 'fraud-ring across IP subnets' signal. Per vin_hash: count(quotes, lifetime), n_unique(policyholder_id, lifetime), count(claims, 365d/lifetime) (insuring or claiming on a VIN that already appears under different policyholders is high signal). Per property_address_hash: count(quotes, lifetime), n_unique(policyholder_id, lifetime), count(prior_losses, 365d/lifetime). Per (claim_id, session): keystroke-dwell distribution (t-digest), mouse-velocity distribution, hesitation count, time-to-first-photo, photo-count, edits-per-field count. Per (policy_id, telematics): rolling 7d/30d/90d aggregates of hard-brake count, phone-handling minutes, night-mileage share, speed-band distribution — the Root / Progressive UBI features. Per peer-network: count(distinct shared-attribute-edges to known-fraud-claim, 90d) (this is fraud-ring graph signal best approximated with HLL or CMS on shared-edge tokens; the deep graph query belongs in a graph DB).
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite and unusually wide for beava. Primary keys typically deployed in parallel: policyholder_id / applicant_id, policy_id, claim_id, device_id (fingerprint), session_id, ip and ip_subnet (/24 or /16), email_hash, email_domain, phone_hash, vin_hash (auto), property_address_hash (home), property_id (Hippo-style sensor grain), member_id (life / health), agent_id (ghost-broker detection), repair_shop_id and medical_provider_id (claims-fraud collusion grain), plus pair grains (device_id, applicant_id), (ip_subnet, 24h_window), (vin_hash, policyholder_id) and (property_address_hash, policyholder_id). FRISS' network analysis explicitly hops across people, vehicles, addresses, phones, VINs, IPs, devices, bank accounts, repair shops and medical providers — beava would store the per-edge counters on each grain and a separate graph DB would run the multi-hop traversal.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate (1h/24h/7d for quote-velocity and FNOL-burst detection; 30d/90d/365d for prior-claim recency, prior-quote recency, telematics rolling aggregates; 3y/lifetime for the prior-claims-on-this-VIN-or-address and prior-claims-on-this-policyholder grains). Tumbling windows show up for the regulator-facing SIU reporting (state insurance commissioner periodic reports, NAIC market-conduct exams). Session windows are load-bearing for the FNOL behavioral session itself — the per-claim_id keystroke / mouse / voice session naturally closes when the claim is submitted, so dwell-ms, edits, hesitation aggregates are session-scoped (not sliding). Exact counters preferred for the application-fraud hard rules and the regulator-facing audit evidence; HLL n_unique acceptable on explosive grains (device_id, ip, email_domain); t-digest for keystroke/mouse/voice-stress distributions.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Mixed but skewed toward auditable. Per-event idempotency keyed by quote_id / claim_id / session_id is acceptable for the velocity counters (slight upward bias from a replay is safe). The claim-decision path requires regulator-grade reproducibility: the feature vector seen by the FNOL fraud model must be snapshotted at decision time and stored alongside the claim record for state insurance commissioner replay, NAIC AI-bulletin audit, and adverse-action notice generation (24+ US states adopted NAIC AI Bulletin substantially by mid-2025, with transparency and accountability as named pillars). This is stricter than card-fraud — a wrongly-denied or wrongly-auto-paid claim has a state regulator complaint pathway that requires producing the exact features the model saw, sometimes years later.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Two distinct budgets. (a) Quote / bind path: ~200 ms–2 s end-to-end is typical (the user is filling a form, and a sub-200 ms feature read inside a 1–2 s quote round-trip is invisible). FRISS markets 'screenings during the seconds it takes to complete an application'. (b) FNOL / claim-decision path: seconds to minutes is acceptable for the end-to-end agentic flow (Shift Claims, Lemonade AI Jim — Lemonade has settled a claim in 2 seconds publicly, with 96% of FNOL handled by AI by end of 2025), but the inner feature-read leg should still be single-digit-ms to fit comfortably inside the agent's tool-call budget. beava's published sub-millisecond TCP+msgpack get / batch_get is well inside both budgets.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Seconds. Quote-velocity features (apps-per-device, apps-per-email-domain, apps-per-VIN) must reflect bursts that complete in seconds to minutes — a 5-minute-stale feature is useless against a ghost-broker script generating 50 synthetic quotes in 60 seconds. FNOL behavioral session features must be available within the agent's tool-call horizon (single-digit seconds). Telematics aggregates (Root, Progressive Snapshot) tolerate minutes-stale because the underwriting decision they feed is periodic (renewal pricing), but real-time hard-brake alerts and crash-detection FNOL-triggers need seconds. beava's push-on-event model gives ms-scale freshness.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Steady-state EPS is moderate for the underwriting / FNOL surface but explosive for the telematics surface. A mid-size carrier handles low thousands of quotes per minute (10s of EPS) and hundreds of FNOLs per hour (sub-1 EPS for claims intake events themselves). Behavioral telemetry inside the FNOL session adds 10–100 events/session × concurrent sessions = low thousands EPS. Telematics is the order-of-magnitude bigger surface: Root analyzes over 10 billion driving miles across its book, with smartphone-SDK sampling typically every 1–30 s per active trip; at scale a Progressive- or Root-sized telematics fleet (1M+ active drivers, peak hours) easily generates 10k–100k EPS sustained. Voice-stress and photo-upload telemetry add bursty 10–50 EPS during FNOL. beava's published 684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack+parallel=16) is comfortably above every part of this profile except a global telematics fleet at peak. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Write-heavy on the telematics and behavioural-session ingest side (one trip = thousands of windowed updates; one FNOL session = hundreds of keystroke / mouse / voice events). Read-balanced on the decision side (one quote or one FNOL pulls 30–100 features via batch_get). Overall, in a Root- or Hippo-style deployment, writes dominate by 1–2 orders of magnitude over reads; in a pure-claims-only Friss / Shift / Charlee deployment, writes and reads are closer to balanced.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Order-of-magnitude per buyer: a mid-size auto carrier with ~5M policyholders × ~6 grains (policyholder, device, vin, ip, email_domain, property) × ~50 features × ~24 B per counter ≈ 30–50 GB hot state for policy / underwriting features. Telematics rolling aggregates (7/30/90 d) at ~10–50 KB per active vehicle for a 1M-active-fleet carrier add another 10–50 GB. FNOL behavioral session state is short-lived (session-window keyed by claim_id, evicted on submit + N hours) and bounded at sub-GB. A regional / mid-market carrier fits cleanly on a single beava box; a top-5 P&C carrier (Allstate, Progressive, USAA, State Farm) will need TTL aggression on the telematics tail or external sharding. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on policyholder_id and policy_id (carriers add 100k–1M new policies/quarter); explosive on device_id, ip and email_hash during application-fraud bursts; bounded on email_domain (low millions globally, long tail dominated by ~100k mainstream domains); bounded on vin_hash globally per market (low hundreds of millions for US auto) but per-carrier it is slowly-growing with the book; bounded on property_address_hash globally per market; bounded on agent_id, repair_shop_id, medical_provider_id (low hundreds of thousands). Telematics trip_id is explosive but each trip naturally evicts after the rolling window. The explosive grains argue for HLL n_unique and aggressive TTL eviction.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Wide range. Quote-velocity counters: 1 h to 90 d. FNOL behavioral session features: minutes to hours (session-scoped, evicted post-decision). Telematics rolling aggregates: 7 / 30 / 90 d hot, 12 months replayable from the SDK backend. Prior-claim recency features: 365 d to 3 y hot, lifetime in the system of record. Application-fraud device / IP / email-domain reputation: 90–180 d. Regulator-grade NAIC / state-DFS / Solvency-II retention runs 7–10 years and is explicitly not beava's job — that lives in a system of record / lakehouse / immutable audit store.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 30–150+ features per decision. Application-fraud rule packs typically pull 30–60 velocity counters across 5–8 grains; FNOL fraud scoring at Lemonade-class carriers pulls 100+ behavioral + telematics + prior-claim features per claim (Lemonade publicly cites time-on-question, answer-revisions, tone, expressions, location, time-of-day, plus full claim-history and prior-policy features as inputs to AI Jim); Friss / Shift / Charlee.ai claim-scoring models combine internal claim features, network-analysis edge features and external enrichment. beava's batch_get / get-many is exactly this shape.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Regulator-grade plus crash-safe at the SIU level. The decision moment must be reproducible: the FNOL feature vector that produced an auto-pay or a SIU escalation has to be snapshottable so a state insurance commissioner or NAIC market-conduct examiner can replay it years later — this is the explicit transparency / accountability pillar of the 2023 NAIC AI Model Bulletin (substantially adopted by 24+ US states by mid-2025). beava's WAL + periodic snapshot covers the crash-safe tier for hot velocity counters; the regulator-grade audit substrate (7–10 yr retention, immutable claim-decision record + features_snapshot) must live in a separate system of record. The refuse-on-network-FS posture is a feature here, not a bug — it prevents the hot tier from accidentally becoming the audit substrate.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary regional / single-binary-per-line-of-business is the natural fit for a mid-market carrier or an insurtech (Lemonade, Hippo, Root, Sezzle-style). Co-located with the FNOL agent runtime, the rules engine (Guidewire / Duck Creek partner ecosystem, FRISS' integration with Guidewire) and the ML scorer inside one VPC. Multi-region active-active is not a hard requirement — claim decisions tolerate seconds, so regional active-passive is acceptable. A top-5 P&C carrier with cross-state operations and per-state regulator residency requirements will hit beava v0's lack of in-process sharding and lack of cross-region replication.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Five personas: (1) the Head of Underwriting / Chief Underwriting Officer at P&C carriers and insurtechs, who owns the quote / bind risk-scoring surface and the agentic-underwriting roadmap that is shifting to continuous (not point-in-time) underwriting in 2026; (2) the Head of SIU / Claims Fraud at carriers and TPAs, who owns the FNOL fraud rules + ML scorer and is the buyer-of-record for Friss, Shift Technology, Charlee.ai, Carpe Data, SAS, FICO, IBM and LexisNexis; (3) the ML platform / data engineering team that operates the feature store under both groups (Lemonade-style 'AI since day one' insurtechs make this a first-class team); (4) the embedded-fraud-vendor itself (Friss, Shift, Charlee.ai, Carpe Data, FormoFraud, Verisk, Quantexa Insurance) as an OEM buyer — beava could be the open-source feature substrate inside a fraud-vendor's product; (5) the Chief Data Officer / Chief Risk Officer for regulator-facing NAIC AI-program documentation and state insurance-commissioner audits.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large and growing. US insurance fraud is estimated at $308.6 B/yr by the Coalition Against Insurance Fraud (2022 study, still the headline figure cited in 2025–2026; P&C ~$45 B, life ~$75 B, Medicare ~$68.7 B, workers' comp ~$34 B). Industry studies repeatedly cite that 25% of claims contain some form of fraud, ~10% of insurance payout dollars lost. The dedicated insurance-fraud-detection software market is sized at ~$6.6–7.2 B in 2025 with ~11% CAGR to $16.9 B by 2034 (Market Research Future / Mordor Intelligence). The agentic-AI-in-insurance subsegment is projected to grow from $5.76 B in 2025 to $7.26 B in 2026 (~26% YoY). Named vendors in this TAM that beava would compete with or under: FICO, SAS, IBM, Experian, LexisNexis, FRISS, SAP, Shift Technology (named AXA Switzerland customer — 3% claims-loss reduction, 30% faster handling, 60% automation, 99% accuracy at FNOL), Charlee.ai (pre-trained on 60M+ claims), Carpe Data, Snapsheet, Five Sigma, Roots Automation. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: Six forces: (1) Loss curve — $308.6 B annual fraud baseline, 25% of claims contain fraud, AI-driven synthetic-identity fraud growing fast (Carpe Data is explicitly campaigning on this in 2025); (2) Regulation — NAIC AI Model Bulletin (Dec 2023) substantially adopted by 24+ US states by Aug 2025, requiring governance, transparency and accountability for any AI used in fraud detection, underwriting or claims; state-DFS NY-style cyber regulation; EU AI Act high-risk classification for insurance pricing and claims; PSD3 / GDPR / CCPA at the data layer. (3) Customer experience pressure — Lemonade has set the bar at 2-second claim settlement and 96% AI-handled FNOL; every legacy carrier now has a board-level mandate to close the gap, and that mandate translates to real-time feature serving. (4) Agentic AI wave — 22% of insurers plan to have an agentic AI solution in production by year-end 2026 (Celent); Shift Claims launched Sep 2025, Duck Creek Agentic AI platform 2026; agents need sub-second feature lookups inside their tool calls. (5) Telematics-driven UBI moving from optional discount to default underwriting — Root, Progressive Snapshot, Allstate Drivewise, State Farm Drive Safe & Save all run continuous streaming features against rolling windows. (6) Litigation crisis — social inflation and litigation funding are pushing carriers to push fraud detection earlier in the lifecycle (FNOL is the cheapest stop point), exactly the wedge Charlee.ai and Carpe Data are selling.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: NAIC Model Bulletin on Use of AI Systems by Insurers (Dec 2023; 24+ states adopted substantially by mid-2025) requires a written AI System Program covering governance, risk management, third-party AI, testing and validation, data lineage, and documentation — the feature vector that produced any adverse action (declined quote, denied claim, escalated SIU) must be reproducible. NAIC Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act (MO-680) at the state level. Solvency II (EU) for capital reserves on claim payouts. EU AI Act (Aug 2024 entered force, high-risk obligations phasing in through 2026) classifies insurance pricing and claims-decision AI as high-risk. UK FCA Consumer Duty applies to consumer insurance products. State-level DFS rules (NY DFS Part 500 cyber; California CCPA for consumer data). HIPAA for health insurance. PCI-DSS for payment-method-token handling. Universal fair-pricing / unfair-discrimination tests (Colorado SB21-169 'algorithmic discrimination in insurance', Texas Department of Insurance scrutiny). 7–10 year claim-file retention is industry-standard. The audit substrate is not beava's job; the regulator wants a reproducible features_snapshot tied to the decision record, which beava can supply at decision time.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: A working application-fraud demo (quotes-per-device, quotes-per-email-domain, quotes-per-VIN with batch_get sub-ms) can stand up on beava in roughly a day, reusing the existing fraud demo schema. A more realistic FNOL behavioral-session demo (keystroke dwell, mouse velocity, time-to-first-photo, prior-claim recency, telematics rolling aggregates) feeding an XGBoost FNOL scorer is a 2–4 week engineering effort. Connecting to a real Guidewire / Duck Creek claims-system FNOL hook with regulator-grade snapshot persistence is a quarter+ effort — most of that work is outside beava (audit substrate, agent runtime, evidence locker), not the feature layer. beava's repo does NOT ship an insurance demo today — python/beava/demos/ has adtech, ecommerce and fraud only; the insurance vertical would be additive.

competition.incumbents: Three layers. (a) Generic online feature stores and streaming engines repositioned for insurance: Chalk (Python-first, real-time, single-digit-ms feature serving; positioned at fintech but the architecture is identical), Tecton (millisecond-to-sub-second feature freshness, fraud detection as a flagship), Hopsworks (real-time ML lakehouse, Clicklease micro-lease underwriting case study), Feast (often Redis-backed), Fennel, Aerospike (used directly as a feature serving store with custom counters). (b) Streaming platforms targeted at insurance claims: Confluent (publicly-named insurance-claims stream-processing reference architecture, claims engine + Flink + Kafka), Materialize, RisingWave, Apache Flink + Kafka (the IJERT 2025 production-ready fraud-pipeline reference). (c) Redis + Lua and Aerospike + custom counters built in-house at every major P&C carrier (USAA + Google Cloud Vertex AI AutoML public case; Allstate's in-house fraud platform — 35% fraud reduction, 92% anomaly detection; Progressive in-house AI with H2O.ai). (d) Generic warehouses-with-streaming (Snowflake Dynamic Tables, Databricks Lakebase) positioning into insurance underwriting.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific incumbents the buyer already integrates with: (a) End-to-end claims-fraud platforms — FRISS (Trust Automation across underwriting / claims / SIU; FICO / IBM / SAS / Experian / LexisNexis / SAP class), Shift Technology (Shift Claims agentic platform; AXA Switzerland customer; FNOL-to-close coverage), Charlee.ai (60M+ claims pre-trained, FNOL Red Flag alerts), Carpe Data (AI-driven fraud focus), Verisk Claims Intelligence, Quantexa for Insurance, SAS Visual Investigator, IBM SPSS Fraud Insurance, Roots Automation, Five Sigma, EIS Digital FNOL. (b) Behavioral biometrics / device intelligence — BioCatch (16B sessions analyzed, expanding into insurance), Feedzai, ThreatMetrix / LexisNexis, IPQS, Fingerprint, Castle, SEON, ForMotiv (insurance-application-specific behavioral analytics), Socure, Persona, Alloy. (c) Voice-stress / video / image analytics — Nuance (now Microsoft), pindrop, deepfake-detection vendors entering the FNOL voice channel. (d) Telematics SDKs — Cambridge Mobile Telematics (CMT, powers Allstate Drivewise / many others), Arity (Allstate), TrueMotion (acquired by CMT), IMS, MOVE, DriveQuant, Damoov. (e) Core systems with embedded fraud — Guidewire ClaimCenter + Shift integration (Shift Accelerator), Duck Creek Agentic AI Platform 2026, Insurity, Sapiens, Snapsheet + Charlee. beava's most direct buyer-side analogue here is Chalk for the feature-substrate role; the most direct OEM analogue is the in-house feature platform that sits under Friss / Shift / Charlee / Carpe Data.
competition.beava_differentiator: Six concrete differentiators: (1) Single binary — no Kafka + Flink + Redis + Feast / Tecton chain; an SIU team or a Friss / Shift / Charlee OEM can stand up real-time velocity and behavioral features in days rather than running a Confluent-class platform migration. (2) 50+ first-class aggregation primitives (count, n_unique, velocity, distance, rate, distribution, t-digest) covering exactly the FNOL / underwriting feature shapes carriers build by hand on Redis + Lua today. (3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits inside the agentic-AI tool-call budget with room for downstream model inference. (4) Push-on-event ingestion via HTTP/JSON and framed TCP+msgpack maps cleanly to mobile SDK (telematics, wearable), web behavioral SDK, voice ingest, and Guidewire / Duck Creek webhook patterns — no Kafka-only assumption. (5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split — an insurtech or an OEM fraud vendor can embed beava without negotiating against a future Enterprise Edition (a problem Confluent, Tecton and Snowflake all face with regulated buyers). (6) Refuse-on-network-FS posture is a feature, not a bug, for a regulated buyer — it prevents accidental drift of the hot tier into being treated as the immutable audit substrate (which is the wrong tool for NAIC retention).
competition.where_beava_loses_today: Concrete gaps that will block production insurance deployments today: (1) No TLS and no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — a NAIC-aligned state-DFS audit will not pass with cleartext feature traffic, even on private subnet; non-negotiable. (2) No multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs — Friss / Shift / Charlee cannot host multiple carrier tenants on one beava box without per-tenant isolation; a top-5 P&C carrier cannot host auto / home / life lines together without it either. (3) No native PII / token-field marking and no built-in per-feature audit log — NAIC AI Bulletin transparency + accountability pillars require evidence of which features touched which protected attributes. (4) No point-in-time coherent snapshot read of the full multi-grain feature vector — every FNOL decision needs a coherent snapshot across policyholder + device + ip + vin + property + telematics grains; an inconsistent composite is an explicit failure mode (Tacnode's real-time decisioning architecture, RisingWave's lending reference both call this out). (5) No in-process sharding and no cross-region replication — a top-5 P&C carrier with per-state regulator residency cannot use one box. (6) No triggers / no 'fire when claims_per_property_address crosses N' — SIU teams want push, not poll. (7) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS — 7–10 year regulatory retention requires a separate system of record; the buyer must accept beava as the hot tier only. (8) No secondary indexes — 'top-N email-domains by quote-velocity in last 24 h' analyst queries are not primary-key gets. (9) No first-class HLL / CMS / t-digest documentation surfaced for the explosive device / IP / email-domain grains and the t-digest keystroke / mouse / voice-stress distributions. (10) No 'features_snapshot_id' primitive that ties together the exact feature vector that produced a particular claim decision for years-long replay — this is the load-bearing NAIC audit requirement. (11) No Guidewire / Duck Creek / Insurity / Sapiens adapter and no FNOL-event-shape starter schema. (12) No image / video / voice perceptual-hash and EXIF-tamper primitives — those are domain-specific signals the buyer expects to bring or have available as a primitive (perceptual_hash, ela_score, exif_tamper_flag would be stored as scalars but the aggregation primitives over them are missing).
competition.integration_surface: Upstream producers: HTTP / mobile-SDK push from telematics SDKs (Cambridge Mobile Telematics / Arity / IMS / MOVE / DriveQuant / Damoov) and from web/mobile FNOL behavioral SDKs (ForMotiv, BioCatch, in-house), webhook from voice-stress / transcript engines, webhooks from photo-upload pipelines, Kafka / Kinesis for buyers with an existing streaming platform, CDC from policy-admin systems (Guidewire PolicyCenter, Duck Creek Policy, Insurity, Sapiens, EIS) and claim-systems (Guidewire ClaimCenter, Duck Creek Claims), webhook from third-party enrichment (LexisNexis, Verisk, FRISS, Shift Accelerator inside Guidewire). beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 and framed TCP+msgpack :8081 map directly to mobile-SDK and webhook patterns; a Kafka/Kinesis consumer adapter is needed and is not in v0. Downstream consumers: an XGBoost / LightGBM FNOL fraud scorer, an agentic-AI orchestrator (Shift Claims-style, Duck Creek Agentic, in-house LangGraph) calling features as tool inputs, a rules engine (Drools, Decision Tables, Guidewire integration profile) for hard SIU policy cutoffs (regulator-flagged repair shops, sanctioned providers, hard velocity limits), and an audit-trail writer (S3 / Postgres / Snowflake / immutable evidence locker) for the decision record + features_snapshot.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, and increasingly an agentic orchestrator on top. The buyer typically runs (a) a rules engine for hard policy cutoffs (sanctioned-provider lists, hard velocity caps, state-specific declines), (b) one or more ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / GBDT for the structured velocity + telematics + behavioral features; transformer / LLM heads for unstructured FNOL transcript / photo / voice signals), and (c) increasingly an agentic AI runtime (Shift Claims, Duck Creek Agentic AI, Lemonade AI Jim, in-house LangGraph) that orchestrates the rules engine and the scorers, calling beava as a tool inside each step. beava is the feature substrate under all three, not the scorer or the agent runtime.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No publicly-named beava users in this domain yet. Comparable published case studies that legitimise the shape: Lemonade — AI Jim handles ~1/3 of claims autonomously, 96% of FNOL by AI by end-2025, 55% of claims fully automated, claim settled in 2 seconds (June 2023 public record); AI Maya end-to-end quote-bind in under 90 s. Shift Technology — AXA Switzerland production deployment of Shift Claims (Sep 2025 launch), reporting 3% claims-loss reduction, 30% faster handling, 60% automation, 99% accuracy; Shift Accelerator inside Guidewire ClaimCenter ecosystem. FRISS — production at tier-1 and tier-2 carriers across underwriting / claims / SIU with fixed-price 6-month go-live SLA. Charlee.ai — pre-trained on 60M+ claims and 50k risk patterns; PCMS strategic ecosystem partner. Allstate — public AI fraud platform with 35% reduction in fraud, 92% anomaly detection accuracy using random forests. adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: High and rising. Application fraud (ghost brokering, synthetic identities, VIN cloning, address spoofing) is actively adversarial and growing with cheap AI tooling — Carpe Data is explicitly campaigning on AI-driven insurance fraud in 2025. FNOL claim fraud is a long-running organized-crime surface (repair-shop / medical-provider collusion rings, staged accidents, exaggerated severity). Deepfake voice and tampered photo / video are emerging FNOL attack surfaces. Feature drift is moderate-to-fast: attackers retool against new SIU rules within weeks. Regulatory model-risk-management cycles dampen how quickly carriers can deploy new features in response, which actually increases the value of a fast-iteration feature substrate that can be A/B'd in shadow before MRM sign-off.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: (1) 7–10 year regulator-grade claim-file retention — that belongs in a warehouse / lakehouse / immutable audit store, not in beava's WAL. (2) The agentic AI runtime itself (LangGraph / Shift Claims / Duck Creek Agentic / in-house) — beava is the feature substrate the agent calls, not the orchestrator. (3) Full claim-text and unstructured-content storage — narrative FNOL transcripts, scanned PDFs, photos and videos belong in object storage; beava stores the derived aggregates and tokens, not the blobs. (4) Cross-policyholder graph traversal ('find every claim within 3 hops of this VIN through any shared device / ip / repair-shop / medical-provider') — this is a graph DB / OLAP problem (Neo4j, TigerGraph, Quantexa, Snowflake), not beava's primary-key get; beava can store the per-edge counters and HLL n_unique on shared-attribute tokens, but the multi-hop traversal lives elsewhere. (5) The fraud / risk scorer itself — XGBoost / LightGBM / LLM heads run in a separate process pulling features via batch_get. (6) Hosting multiple carrier tenants on one box — no multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs in v0. (7) Regulator-grade affordability / fair-pricing evidence retention — beava supplies the hot features and snapshot id; the audit substrate is separate. (8) Telematics raw trip storage and historical replay over 12+ months — the SDK backend keeps that; beava holds the rolling 7/30/90 d aggregates.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for insurance underwriting / FNOL at a regulated carrier or an embedded fraud-vendor OEM: (1) TLS on all three listeners (:8080, :8081, :8090) plus mTLS option — non-negotiable for state-DFS / NAIC / SOC 2 / EU AI Act audit posture. (2) AuthN / AuthZ — at minimum API-key auth scoped per namespace, ideally JWT / OIDC integration; per-feature read/write ACLs for separation of duty between SIU, claims-ops and underwriting. (3) Point-in-time coherent snapshot read of a multi-grain feature vector — needed for the auditable features_snapshot_id that ties an FNOL decision to the exact features the model and the agent saw, including across policyholder / device / ip / vin / property / telematics / behavioral grains simultaneously. (4) A built-in append-only decision-record sink (Kafka / S3 / Postgres CDC out) so the carrier can persist (decision_id, claim_id, features_snapshot, model_version, decision, reason_codes) without writing glue. (5) Triggers / event-driven actions — 'when claims_per_property_address > N in 365 d, emit a SIU alert', 'when quotes_per_email_domain crosses N in 24 h, lock further binds', 'when telematics_phone_handling_minutes_7d > threshold, schedule renewal step-up' — SIU and claims-ops teams want push, not poll. (6) Multi-tenancy with hard namespace isolation and per-tenant quotas so an OEM fraud vendor (Friss / Shift / Charlee / Carpe Data) or a multi-line carrier (auto / home / pet / life) can host programs on one box. (7) In-process sharding and consistent-hashing across entities so a top-5 P&C carrier can scale within one cluster without external hand-sharding. (8) Cross-region replication (active-passive with bounded staleness is acceptable). (9) First-class approximate-aggregate primitives surfaced and documented — HLL n_unique on device / ip / email-domain explosive grains, CMS top-K on 'most-claim-heavy property addresses in last 90 d', t-digest for keystroke / mouse / voice-stress / telematics-speed distributions. (10) Configurable per-feature TTLs and eviction so 90-d behavioural-reputation features can coexist with 1-h quote-velocity counters, 7-d telematics aggregates and 3-y prior-claim recency. (11) Explicit PII / token-field marking and per-feature audit log — NAIC AI Bulletin transparency and accountability pillars require evidence of which features touched protected-class attributes. (12) Secondary index / scan API for SIU analyst queries ('top-N email-domains by quote-velocity last 24 h', 'top-N repair-shops by claim-count last 90 d'). (13) Image / video / voice perceptual-hash and EXIF-tamper primitives wired into the table grammar so the FNOL photo / voice pipeline can store and aggregate on perceptual_hash, ela_score, voice_stress_score with the same ergonomic story as count / velocity. (14) Reference integrations / Guidewire ClaimCenter and Duck Creek Claims event-bridge adapters and a telematics-SDK ingest adapter (CMT / Arity / IMS). (15) An insurance demo under `python/beava/demos/insurance/` with FNOL + quote + telematics + behavioral session shapes — closest to the existing `fraud/` demo, additive in scope.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes, materially. SIU and underwriting ops both want push: 'when claims_per_property_address > N in 365 d, fire a SIU alert', 'when quotes_per_email_domain crosses N in 24 h, block further binds and notify fraud-ops', 'when telematics_hard_brake_count_7d > threshold, schedule renewal step-up', 'when fnol behavioural session keystroke-dwell-stddev is in the top decile and prior-claim-recency < 30 d, escalate to manual review'. Today beava cannot do this natively — the buyer must poll. The synchronous decision-time path (quote auth, FNOL auto-pay) tolerates poll because the read is happening anyway. The asynchronous SIU / underwriting-renewal / agent-of-record alert paths are wasteful without native triggers, and this is the most-cited gap in the adjacent fraud and account-abuse domains. The regulator-grade reproducibility requirement (features_snapshot_id) is itself effectively a trigger-on-decision — every claim decision should be able to materialize a coherent feature vector and emit it downstream to the audit substrate.
